records.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders

records.question: How many unique customers have placed an order?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

records.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo (SP)?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) AS seller_count FROM sellers WHERE seller_state = 'SP'

records.question: What is the average review score?
records.sql: SELECT AVG(review_score) AS avg_review_score FROM order_reviews

records.question: How many orders were canceled?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS canceled_orders FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'canceled'

records.question: How many payments were made with each payment type?
records.sql: SELECT payment_type, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY payment_count DESC

records.question: What is the most common number of instalments for credit card payments?
records.sql: SELECT payment_installments, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM order_payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card' GROUP BY payment_installments ORDER BY payment_count DESC LIMIT 1

records.question: How many orders were placed in 2017?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_2017 FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01'

records.question: How many reviews were given at each review score?
records.sql: SELECT review_score, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM order_reviews GROUP BY review_score ORDER BY review_score

records.question: What is the total payment value for each payment type?
records.sql: SELECT payment_type, SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY total_payment_value DESC

records.question: What are the top 5 product categories by revenue? Use English category names.
records.sql: SELECT COALESCE(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Which 5 customer states placed the most orders?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Which 5 customer states have the longest average delivery time in days?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, AVG(date_diff('second', o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_delivered_customer_date) / 86400.0) AS avg_delivery_days FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY avg_delivery_days DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Who are the top 10 sellers by revenue?
records.sql: SELECT oi.seller_id, s.seller_city, s.seller_state, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS num_orders FROM order_items oi LEFT JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_city, s.seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10
records.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'revenue'

records.question: Which 5 customer states have the highest average order value?
records.sql: WITH order_values AS (SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_state, SUM(p.payment_value) AS order_value FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, c.customer_state) SELECT customer_state, ROUND(AVG(order_value), 2) AS avg_order_value, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM order_values GROUP BY customer_state ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC LIMIT 5
records.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'aov'

records.question: For each review score, what is the average delivery time in days?
records.sql: SELECT r.review_score, AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0) AS avg_delivery_days, COUNT(*) AS num_orders FROM order_reviews r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.review_score ORDER BY r.review_score

records.question: Which 5 product categories have the highest average freight value per item? Use English names.
records.sql: SELECT COALESCE(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category, AVG(oi.freight_value) AS avg_freight_value, COUNT(*) AS item_count FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name WHERE p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg_freight_value DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Which 5 seller states sold the most items?
records.sql: SELECT s.seller_state, COUNT(*) AS items_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id GROUP BY s.seller_state ORDER BY items_sold DESC LIMIT 5
records.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'items_sold'

records.question: On average, how many items does an order contain?
records.sql: SELECT AVG(item_count) AS avg_items_per_order FROM (SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS item_count FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) t

records.question: How many orders were placed in each month from January to August 2018?
records.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: How have sales trended month by month?
records.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue, SUM(oi.price + oi.freight_value) AS revenue_incl_freight FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: What percentage of customers are repeat customers?
records.sql: WITH per_customer AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_customers, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_count > 1) AS repeat_customers, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_count > 1) / COUNT(*), 2) AS repeat_customer_pct FROM per_customer
records.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'repeat_pct'

records.question: What share of delivered orders arrived later than the estimated delivery date, by month in 2018?
records.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_share_pct FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2019-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: What was the month-over-month revenue growth rate in 2018, from February to August?
records.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01' AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY 1), g AS (SELECT month, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_revenue FROM monthly) SELECT strftime(month, '%Y-%m') AS month, revenue, prev_revenue, ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - prev_revenue) / prev_revenue, 2) AS mom_growth_pct FROM g WHERE month >= TIMESTAMP '2018-02-01' AND month < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01' ORDER BY month

records.question: Do late deliveries get worse reviews? Compare the average review score of late and on-time delivered orders.
records.sql: WITH delivered AS (SELECT order_id, CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END AS delivery_status FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL), order_scores AS (SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score FROM order_reviews WHERE review_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY order_id) SELECT d.delivery_status, COUNT(*) AS num_orders, ROUND(AVG(s.score), 3) AS avg_review_score FROM delivered d JOIN order_scores s ON d.order_id = s.order_id GROUP BY d.delivery_status ORDER BY d.delivery_status

records.question: Among product categories with at least 1,000 reviewed orders, which 5 have the lowest average review score? Use English names.
records.sql: WITH order_review AS (SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score FROM order_reviews WHERE review_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY order_id), order_cat AS (SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id, COALESCE(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name WHERE p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL) SELECT oc.category, COUNT(DISTINCT oc.order_id) AS reviewed_orders, ROUND(AVG(r.score), 3) AS avg_review_score FROM order_cat oc JOIN order_review r ON oc.order_id = r.order_id GROUP BY oc.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oc.order_id) >= 1000 ORDER BY avg_review_score ASC LIMIT 5

records.question: Among customer states with at least 1,000 delivered orders, which has the highest late delivery rate?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders, AVG(CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS late_rate FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000 ORDER BY late_rate DESC LIMIT 1

records.question: What share of total revenue comes from the top 10% of sellers?
records.sql: WITH seller_rev AS (SELECT seller_id, SUM(price) AS revenue FROM order_items GROUP BY seller_id), ranked AS (SELECT seller_id, revenue, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM seller_rev) SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN rn <= CEIL(n * 0.1) THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS top10_revenue, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN rn <= CEIL(n * 0.1) THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / SUM(revenue) AS top10_share FROM ranked

records.question: For customers who ordered more than once, what is the average number of days between their first and second order?
records.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_id) AS rn FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL), pairs AS (SELECT customer_unique_id, MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN order_purchase_timestamp END) AS first_ts, MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 2 THEN order_purchase_timestamp END) AS second_ts FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 2 GROUP BY customer_unique_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS repeat_customers, AVG(epoch(second_ts - first_ts) / 86400.0) AS avg_days_between_first_and_second_order FROM pairs WHERE second_ts IS NOT NULL

records.question: Which 5 product categories grew revenue the most from 2017 to 2018? Compare January to August of each year, in absolute terms, using English names.
records.sql: WITH rev AS (SELECT COALESCE(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name, 'unknown') AS category, SUM(CASE WHEN year(o.order_purchase_timestamp)=2017 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2017, SUM(CASE WHEN year(o.order_purchase_timestamp)=2018 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2018 FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON oi.product_id=p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name=ct.product_category_name WHERE year(o.order_purchase_timestamp) IN (2017,2018) AND month(o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN 1 AND 8 AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled','unavailable') GROUP BY 1) SELECT category, revenue_2017, revenue_2018, revenue_2018 - revenue_2017 AS revenue_growth FROM rev ORDER BY revenue_growth DESC LIMIT 5
